articles.title: 'For Americans only': US launches nationwide crackdown on illegal immigrants over food aid fraud; several arrested
articles.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security has initiated a major crackdown on undocumented immigrants accused of fraudulently obtaining food assistance via the SNAP program, leading to multiple arrests.
articles.body: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has launched a nationwide operation targeting undocumented immigrants accused of fraudulently obtaining food assistance through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), with several arrests reported by federal authorities.US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) confirmed the arrests to Fox News. DHS said those detained include nationals of Haiti and Cuba who were allegedly living in the US illegally and had accessed the federally funded assistance programme.Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended the operation, arguing that people living in the country unlawfully should not receive taxpayer-funded benefits.“Illegal aliens who have no right to be here in the first place are the last people who should be using SNAP benefits and other forms of welfare,” Mullin said in a statement.“These programs are for Americans only,” he added, saying that even non-violent offences involving undocumented immigrants could have serious consequences when they involve alleged fraud against taxpayers.Mullin described those already apprehended and deported as “just a drop in the bucket”, indicating that the Trump administration intended to pursue further cases.Among those identified by DHS is Rubstony Junior Theodore, a Haitian national accused of living in the US unlawfully. ICE arrested him as part of the operation, according to federal officials. DHS said his criminal history includes arrests for larceny, obstruction of officers and trespassing.Three other Haitian nationals, Wilbert Jean Baptiste, Louis Jean and Jhensly Charles, were also arrested, the agency said.Authorities also identified Elizabeth Povea Rodriguez, a Cuban national accused of residing in the country illegally. She had previously been convicted of disorderly conduct and had been arrested over allegations involving battery and domestic violence.The department described the arrests as the beginning of a wider enforcement effort focused on alleged misuse of SNAP benefits.“These arrests mark the opening salvo in a sustained, large-scale ICE operation specifically targeting illegal aliens who have fraudulently accessed SNAP benefits that American taxpayers fund exclusively for US citizens in need,” DHS said.You use AI every day. articles.title: eMudhra security breach explained: What it is and means for smartphone, internet users
articles.summary: In another security incident, researchers have found that eight digital certificates issued by the Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra were protected by
articles.body: In another security incident, researchers have found that eight digital certificates issued by the Indian cybersecurity company eMudhra were protected by secret keys so weak that they could be cracked in less than a second. Google, Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla have now blocked the certificates. So far, there is no evidence that anyone used the flaw to carry out an attack. While some are asking how such a basic mistake got through in the first place and how long it will take to clean up across the internet, a majority is trying to understand why this matters, how they are impacted and what they should do to keep themselves safe. Here’s the security incident explained.What is eMudhra and what does it doLet’s start with an example. Every time you open a website, your browser has to check that it is talking to the real site and not an imposter. It does this using digital certificates, which work like ID cards for websites. There are companies that issue these ID cards. They are called Certificate Authorities, and eMudhra is one of them – an Indian digital trust and cybersecurity company. It sells certificates under the emSign brand through companies in India, the United States and the Netherlands. Major browsers keep a list of companies they trust, and eMudhra is on the lists of Mozilla (Firefox), Chrome (Google) and Safari (Apple).In a real world scenario, consider you want to buy an iPhone. You can either buy it from the Apple Store or retail partners that are authorised to sell those phones which means that you will get a product that meets the highest standard. In the certificate world, consider these retail partners as intermediate certificates. Each one has a secret key, which works like Apple’s official stamp. Anyone who holds the stamp can issue IDs that look genuine to everyone else.What exactly happenedeMudhra created eight of these intermediate certificates last year. Six were meant for websites and two were meant for signing software. The secret key for each should have been an enormous random number, one with around 1 followed by 115 zeros possible values. Instead, the keys turned out to be tiny numbers. One was simply the number 4, and the others were 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.To understand this, think of a padlock. A good one has so many possible combinations that nobody could ever try them all. These keys were like a padlock with only 256 possible combinations, which can be opened by trying every one in a blink. Researchers recovered all eight keys in less than a second.The keys were not stolen. Google’s security teams said they were created with too little randomness, so anyone can work them out from the public certificates. eMudhra says a flaw in the April 2025 process that created the certificates produced a second, weak set of keys alongside the intended strong ones, and the weak set is what got published to the browser lists.Why it mattersIf someone held these keys, they could issue a certificate for any website that a browser would accept. In everyday terms, you could land on what looks like your bank’s website or a shopping site and have no idea you are connected to a fake one. Your browser would see nothing wrong. An attacker could also read or tamper with the information, including sensitive details, passing between you and a website.A researcher reported the problem to the browser companies on October 17. To prove it, the researcher signed a message with each of the eight keys. Chrome and Firefox blocked the certificates within hours. Apple blocked them on October 19 and Microsoft on October 20. Android phones got a similar block through Google Play Services on October 19. eMudhra has revoked the eight certificates, and Cloudflare and other software providers have released fixes.According to the company, there is no evidence so far that the weak keys were used in a cyberattack, though it is not known for certain whether anyone misused them since they were created. Chrome said that, before it blocked them, no website certificates issued through the six website certificates had been recorded in the public logs it requires. That means Chrome and similar browsers would not have trusted such certificates by default.What eMudhra has to sayIn a statement, eMudhra said the problem was limited to these intermediate certificates and did not affect its main root keys or its other intermediate certificates. It added that only one of the eight had been put to use, and that none of the eight had issued a certificate to any individual website. The company also said its systems were not hacked and no data was breached. It said its Indian digital signature and eSign businesses run on separate systems and are not connected to the incident.What this means for eMudhraOn October 20, Mozilla removed one of eMudhra’s main roots (emSign ECC Root CA - G3) from its trusted list. Chrome will remove the same root in its next update to its trusted list. That removal is expected to reach devices on the morning of Tuesday, October 27, Pacific time. Chrome is also reviewing eMudhra’s other main root, citing the seriousness of the incident. Website owners whose certificates depend on that root must switch to a certificate from another provider before then to avoid problems. Google says eMudhra has committed to moving those customers.How are everyday users affected, and what should they doFor most people, nothing much is needed. Browsers get these blocks pushed to them automatically, and Chrome and Firefox did not need a manual update or a restart. The best thing that users can do is to keep their browsers, phone and apps up to date so they have the latest fixes. Don’t try to change certificate settings.Some software is a different story. Many programs, mostly tools used by developers and companies, do not receive these blocks automatically and keep trusting a certificate until the software itself is updated. Cloudflare has warned that customers who run their own servers or systems may need to update them by hand. Mozilla has also warned that some websites and servers may stop working for users of software that relies on its list until they move to new certificates.You use AI every day. articles.title: Zelensky says he’d be open to freezing front lines to end Russia war
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday said he would be open to freezing the front line of his forces to allow the war with Russia to end and keep much of Ukraine’s territory intact. “Right now, we have to freeze, and I think this is a real way to end this war,” Zelensky told “Fox…
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday said he would be open to freezing the front line of his forces to allow the war with Russia to end and keep much of Ukraine’s territory intact.

“Right now, we have to freeze, and I think this is a real way to end this war,” Zelensky told “Fox & Friends” co-host Brian Kilmeade on Fox News . “We call [for the] ceasefire, or stop killing stuff, like President Trump called it. Freeze and stop. And, of course, this is the minimum of what we need from Russia today.”

Zelensky said Ukraine will go to President Trump and European leaders to ask for security guarantees, which he said were “most important.”

The Ukrainian leader resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries after Trump announced an energy ceasefire between the warring countries earlier this month, claiming they were in retaliation for Russian strikes shortly after the announcement.

Zelensky’s remarks preceded Russian President Vladimir Putin’s agreement on Wednesday to resume trilateral negotiations with Washington and Kyiv to end the nearly five-year-long war, Kremlin spokesperson Yuri Ushakov told The Associated Press after a three-hour meeting between Putin and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff.

Ushakov said Putin agreed to resume trilateral talks “in principle” after Nov. 10.

It was during this meeting that Witkoff announced that Russia agreed to release U.S. teacher Stephen Hubbard, who was sentenced to prison in 2024 after Russian prosecutors accused him of fighting alongside Ukraine against Russia as a mercenary, a claim Hubbard denied.

Republican senators have panned the idea of Trump meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping to cut a peace deal that Ukraine would be forced to accept. Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) stressed that Ukraine should be part of the trilateral talks to end the war, saying Kyiv’s absence in the talks would be “nonsense.”

The push to end the conflict frayed in recent weeks as Trump, seeking to address the energy shortage instigated by the U.S.-Israeli conflict in Iran, struck a deal with the Kremlin to allow diesel into the U.S. and waived sanctions on Russia.

Bipartisan lawmakers blasted the waiver, as Trump said it “immediately” went into effect weeks after he signed a legislative package that placed further sanctions on Russia, which was passed by Congress in a bill named after the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.).

They also lambasted the diesel deal, with Zelensky advising the U.S. not to make a “ historic mistake ” by supporting Russia.

articles.title: GOP rep: ‘We got to investigate’ Starlink slowdown report
articles.summary: Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.) is calling for a congressional investigation into the Starlink slowdown in Ukraine after a report that SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk personally ordered it. “We got to call the witnesses, got to bring them in, put them under oath, and get to the bottom of it,” Fitzpatrick told CNN’s…
articles.body:
Republican Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.) is calling for a congressional investigation into the Starlink slowdown in Ukraine after a report that SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk personally ordered it.

“We got to call the witnesses, got to bring them in, put them under oath, and get to the bottom of it,” Fitzpatrick told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on Tuesday. “We cannot just move past this. This is a serious, serious issue because lapsing Starshield in that manner that costs human lives, there’s got to be consequences to that.”

The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that Musk directed the slowdown of Starshield, a military version of his Starlink internet owned and operated by the U.S. government. Ukrainian forces use Starshield as part of their efforts to defend the country from Russian attacks.

The move sparked bipartisan backlash on the heels of President Trump’s recent efforts to put distance between the U.S. and Ukraine, including waiving sanctions on Russian energy and calling for the replacement of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Fitzpatrick said Tuesday he spoke to several other lawmakers about investigating the slowdown once the House returns to Washington.

“I’ve spoken to several of my colleagues across the aisle over the past several days,” Fitzpatrick said. “There is a strong, strong resolve to immediately upon our return get to the bottom of this through oversight, and there’s got to be consequences.”

The Pennsylvania Republican, who co-chairs the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and once lived in the embattled country, is locked in a tough reelection battle in a district former Vice President Kamala Harris won in 2024. He has been one of the more willing GOP members of Congress to criticize Trump when the administration does something he disagrees with.

In Tuesday’s interview, Fitzpatrick threatened financial consequences for any federal agencies that may have had knowledge of the slowdown and Musk’s role.

“The executive branch of government does not have a dime of their own money in their own right. The taxpayer money is sent to them through the legislative branch, and there needs to be financial consequences to any agency or any agency head that had any part in this,” Fitzpatrick said.

He also called responses from executive branch officials “wildly insufficient.”

“There’s a lot of finger pointing, a lot of people saying, ‘Well, not me.’ OK, if not you, then who? Right? They have the ability inside the executive branch to determine where the problem was, identify the person, identify the policy … we have to get to the answer,” the lawmaker added.

articles.title: Macron assails ‘unacceptable and even stupid’ remarks from Trump, others on France riots
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday blasted the “unacceptable and even stupid” remarks made by President Trump and others claiming student riots in France are the result of immigration. “We have people who explained that we have been invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is totally false,” Macron told reporters in Doha, Qatar,…
articles.body:
French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday blasted the “unacceptable and even stupid” remarks made by President Trump and others claiming student riots in France are the result of immigration.

“We have people who explained that we have been invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is totally false,” Macron told reporters in Doha, Qatar, in translated remarks from Al Jazeera . “For me, there is no visible foreign interference in the events that took place. On the other hand, there was foreign manipulation of information which led to unacceptable and even stupid comments by many, including foreign leaders.”

When asked by reporters if that included Trump’s comments, Macron said, “Among others, but he is part of it.”

“You know, at times like this you see who loves France and who does not,” he continued. “All the people –– it has to be said –– all the people who are running down our country right now are people who don’t love our country. So these people get on my nerves.”

Macron condemned violence that has spiraled out of the massive demonstrations, some of which have turned into rioting on city streets. He said the government’s objective now is “to hear and respect the concerns, the disagreements, sometimes the anger that is there to address their root causes to do so in an orderly manner.”

“But to separate them from the violence that has taken place, to which we will concede nothing,” he added.

On Saturday, more than half a million people took to the streets calling for better conditions in schools and demanding action on the high cost of living. French officials said they have arrested at least 2,500 people in connection with riots in some parts of the country.

Trump, Vice President Vance and right-wing leaders across Europe have blamed the protests on mass migration from the Middle East and Africa to Europe. Trump has attempted to tie these protests to what he claims could happen in the U.S. if Democrats win majorities in Congress after the midterm elections.

Vance on Monday shared a video of a 150-year-old town hall burning in France on social media and said he hoped “Americans are paying attention.”

“This is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country,” the vice president wrote.

Trump has also sought to tie the French protests to his economic messaging in the weeks remaining before the midterms, though polling has shown his economic policies have grown unpopular among Americans.

“When I go to North Carolina, today I’m going to be speaking about it. But Europe has to change its ways or you’re not going to have Europe left,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office on Tuesday ahead of a campaign rally in Greenville, N.C.
